deities.name: Fertility & Birth
deities.blurb: Powers over conception, childbirth and the increase of families and herds - appealed to more often, and by more people, than the sky gods.

deities.name: Kingship & Justice
deities.blurb: Divine authority and the law it underwrites - the gods a ruler claimed descent from, and the ones who judged the ruler.

deities.name: Agriculture & Harvest
deities.blurb: The gods standing behind the farming year - planting, rain on the crop, the grain in the store, and the prosperity that follows a good one.

deities.name: Creation & Origins
deities.blurb: The first powers - those who made the world, or were the world before anything was made of it.

deities.name: Magic & Prophecy
deities.blurb: Those who see what has not happened yet, and those who change what has.

deities.name: Protection & Guardianship
deities.blurb: Warders of doors, roads, households and children - the everyday gods, appealed to most often.

deities.name: Death & the Underworld
deities.blurb: Rulers and wardens of the land of the dead, judges of souls, and the guides who carry the newly dead across.

deities.name: Earth & Wilderness
deities.blurb: The ground itself, the mountains standing on it, and the wild country beyond the last field.

deities.name: Sea & Waters
deities.blurb: Ocean powers, river spirits and the gods sailors bargained with.

deities.name: Sun, Moon & Stars
deities.blurb: The lights that keep time - solar and lunar deities, dawn-bringers, and the powers behind the constellations.

deities.name: War & Battle
deities.blurb: Gods who decide the outcome of fighting - patrons of armies, personifications of the battle rage, and the powers soldiers prayed to before a line advanced.

deities.name: Sky, Storm & Thunder
deities.blurb: Thunderers and sky-fathers: the weather as an expression of divine temper.

deities.name: Wisdom & Knowledge
deities.blurb: Patrons of writing, counsel and memory - the gods invoked before a difficult decision rather than a difficult journey.

deities.name: Healing & Medicine
deities.blurb: Physicians among the gods - and the same powers, often, that sent the disease.

deities.name: Love & Desire
deities.blurb: Powers of attraction, marriage and longing - and of the trouble that follows them.

deities.name: Craft & Fire
deities.blurb: Smiths, makers and the fire they work with - the gods of everything built rather than grown.

deities.name: Tricksters & Chaos
deities.blurb: The gods who break the rules the other gods depend on - and are tolerated because the world would seize up without them.

creatures.name: Shapeshifters
creatures.blurb: Creatures with no fixed form - the largest single ability in the whole bestiary, and the hardest to defend against.

creatures.name: Tricksters & Deceivers
creatures.blurb: Creatures that beat you with misdirection rather than force - illusion-casters, mimics and things wearing a friendly face.

creatures.name: Forest & Wild Places
creatures.blurb: The oldest fear in the collection: whatever is in the trees once you are past the edge of the village.

creatures.name: Mountains & Caves
creatures.blurb: Things that live under stone, or above the treeline where nobody farms.

creatures.name: Water Dwellers
creatures.blurb: What waits in rivers, lakes and the open sea - drowners, luring singers and things too large to see whole.

creatures.name: Night Terrors
creatures.blurb: Nocturnal predators and the things blamed for sleep paralysis, blood loss and children who did not come home.

creatures.name: Winged & Airborne
creatures.blurb: Creatures that get above you - from feathered messengers to things that carry off cattle.

creatures.name: Undead & Restless Spirits
creatures.blurb: The dead who did not stay dead, and what they want from the living.

creatures.name: Guardians & Watchers
creatures.blurb: Set to watch a door, a hoard or a boundary - and not to be reasoned with.

creatures.name: Giants & Titans
creatures.blurb: The oversized - often older than the gods, and usually losing to them.

creatures.name: Dragons & Serpents
creatures.blurb: The coiled shape that nearly every tradition arrived at independently - hoarder, world-encircler, and the thing heroes are measured against.

creatures.name: Hybrid Beasts
creatures.blurb: Assembled creatures - part lion, part eagle, part something that should not join to either.

heroes.name: Warriors & Champions
heroes.blurb: Fighters who stood for an army, a city or a cause.

heroes.name: Founders & Kings
heroes.blurb: Heroes a city, a dynasty or a people claimed as their beginning.

heroes.name: Tragic Figures
heroes.blurb: Heroes undone by the quality that made them heroes.

heroes.name: Sages & Teachers
heroes.blurb: Those remembered for what they knew and passed on.

heroes.name: Culture Bringers
heroes.blurb: The ones who brought fire, writing, law or agriculture - and usually paid for it.

heroes.name: Voyagers & Questers
heroes.blurb: Those sent a long way for a single object - and changed more by the journey than the prize.

heroes.name: Demigods & Divine Blood
heroes.blurb: Born of a god and a mortal, and at home in neither world.

heroes.name: Ancestors & Progenitors
heroes.blurb: Heroes a people traced their descent from.

heroes.name: Tricksters & Outlaws
heroes.blurb: Heroes who win by wit, theft or nerve rather than by arms.

heroes.name: Monster Slayers
heroes.blurb: The oldest job description in myth: something is eating the countryside, and one person goes out to it.

items.name: Legendary Weapons
items.blurb: Named blades, spears and hammers - usually better known than the hands that held them.

items.name: Healing Relics
items.blurb: Objects that mend, restore or refuse to let the holder die.

items.name: Crowns & Regalia
items.blurb: The objects that made a claim to rule legible - and were fought over accordingly.

items.name: Rings, Amulets & Charms
items.blurb: Small worn things carrying power out of proportion to their size.

items.name: Vessels & Cauldrons
items.blurb: Cups, cauldrons and jars that never empty, or hold something that should not be let out.

items.name: Instruments & Music
items.blurb: Harps, flutes and horns that move armies, wake the dead or open the earth.

items.name: Mirrors, Keys & Portals
items.blurb: Objects that open a way - to another place, another time, or the truth.

items.name: Armour & Shields
items.blurb: What stood between a hero and the thing trying to kill him.

items.name: Cursed Objects
items.blurb: Things that cost the holder more than they gave - and could not simply be put down.

items.name: Books & Tablets
items.blurb: Written objects treated as powers in themselves - scrolls, tablets and books of names.

places.name: Temples & Shrines
places.blurb: Built places where a tradition's practice actually happened.

places.name: Sacred Waters
places.blurb: Rivers, wells and springs credited with purifying, healing or remembering.

places.name: Realms of the Dead
places.blurb: Where the dead go, how they are judged there, and what it costs to visit and return.

places.name: Divine Realms & Heavens
places.blurb: The homes of the gods - usually above, usually hard to reach, occasionally visited.

places.name: Thresholds & Gateways
places.blurb: Crossings between worlds - bridges, gates and the rivers you are ferried over.

places.name: Gardens & Paradises
places.blurb: Enclosed perfect places - almost always with one rule attached.

places.name: Sacred Mountains
places.blurb: High ground treated as the meeting point of the human and the divine.

places.name: Lost Cities & Ruins
places.blurb: Places remembered as having fallen - and sometimes argued about as having existed.

concepts.name: Conspiracy Theories
concepts.blurb: Claims of concealed coordination — who is said to be hiding what, and the evidence offered for it.

concepts.name: Alternative Science
concepts.blurb: Theories offered in place of the scientific consensus, from free energy to suppressed inventions.

concepts.name: Ancient Mysteries
concepts.blurb: Unexplained construction, artefacts and knowledge attributed to the deep past.

concepts.name: Religious Mysteries
concepts.blurb: Disputed relics, hidden scripture and the claims built around them.

concepts.name: UFOs & Contact
concepts.blurb: Sightings, abduction accounts and the institutions said to have handled them.

concepts.name: Paranormal
concepts.blurb: Hauntings, psychic claims and phenomena reported outside physical explanation.

concepts.name: Spiritual Practice
concepts.blurb: Disciplines and beliefs concerned with inner transformation.

concepts.name: Cryptids
concepts.blurb: Creatures reported but never catalogued — the modern bestiary.

concepts.name: Cosmological Claims
concepts.blurb: Assertions about the shape, origin and governance of the universe.

concepts.name: Alternative History
concepts.blurb: Accounts of the past that depart from the documented record.

concepts.name: Philosophical
concepts.blurb: Ideas argued rather than evidenced — the questions underneath the claims.

concepts.name: Secret Societies
concepts.blurb: Orders and fraternities, their real history and the influence attributed to them.

concepts.name: Lost Civilisations
concepts.blurb: Atlantis, Lemuria and the other vanished worlds people keep looking for.

concepts.name: Ritual Practice
concepts.blurb: Rites and ceremonies recorded as practice rather than belief.

regions.name: Classical Mediterranean
regions.blurb: Greece and Rome, and the Etruscans they borrowed from - the best-documented pantheons in the collection, and the template most Western readers measure the others against.

regions.name: East Asia
regions.blurb: China, Japan and Korea - three traditions that borrowed from each other continuously and stayed distinct.

regions.name: Ancient Near East
regions.blurb: Sumer, Babylon, Assyria, Canaan and Persia - the oldest written myths anywhere, and the source of flood and creation stories that travelled a long way.

regions.name: Celtic & Insular
regions.blurb: Ireland, Wales, Scotland and Brittany, plus the Arthurian material that grew out of them and outgrew them.

regions.name: South Asia
regions.blurb: Hindu, Buddhist and Jain traditions - the largest living mythologies here, still in daily practice rather than only in texts.

regions.name: The Americas
regions.blurb: Aztec, Maya and Inca, and the many North American nations - traditions that survived deliberate attempts to erase them.

regions.name: Norse & Germanic
regions.blurb: The northern pantheon and its cousins - a mythology preserved largely by people writing it down after they had stopped believing it.

regions.name: Egypt & the Nile
regions.blurb: Three thousand years of a single tradition, unusually concerned with what happens after death and unusually specific about it.

regions.name: Southeast Asia & the Pacific
regions.blurb: Island traditions across an ocean - Polynesian voyaging myth, Aboriginal Dreaming, and the archipelago cultures between them.

regions.name: Abrahamic Traditions
regions.blurb: Jewish, Christian and Islamic material - scripture, apocrypha, and the angels and demons that accumulated around them.

regions.name: Northern & Eastern Europe
regions.blurb: Slavic, Baltic and Finno-Ugric traditions - forest mythologies, recorded late and often only in folk song.

regions.name: Africa
regions.blurb: Yoruba, Akan, Zulu and the diaspora traditions carried to the Americas - among the most under-recorded material in the collection.

regions.name: Western Europe
regions.blurb: French, Iberian and Alpine folklore - the local traditions that persisted under Christianity rather than being replaced by it.

regions.name: Esoteric & Occult
regions.blurb: Tarot, alchemy, hermeticism and the Western magical tradition - systems that borrowed gods from everywhere and rearranged them.
